rules.name: Sources and Methods Seminar (HISTORY 1S-99S)
rules.notes: The Sources and Methods seminar should be taken as early as possible in a student’s course of study. Ideally, it should be taken before the Doing History course (below) and it must be taken before enrolling in HISTORY209S Research Seminar for Majors (below).

rules.name: Doing History Colloquium (HISTORY 200x)
rules.notes:
Students are strongly encouraged to satisfy their “Doing History” requirement before the end of their sophomore year.
Optional additional "Doing History" colloquia may count toward the 200-level undergraduate colloquium requirement (see below).

rules.name: 200-level Undergraduate Colloquia (HISTORY 201-298)
rules.notes: Must be taken for a minimum of three units.

rules.name: 13 Courses and 63 Units
rules.desc: Students must complete a minimum of 13 courses and 63 units in the major.

rules.name: Concentration
rules.notes:
History majors must complete four courses in a geographic (e.g., Africa, the United States) chronological (e.g., ancient, early modern), or thematic concentration.
Thematic concentrations include, but are not limited to:

• Global Affairs and International Relations

• Law and Public Policy

• Environment, Science, Medicine and Technology

• Economics and Political Economy

• Religion and Intellectual History

• Activism, Public History and Public Service

• Gender and Sexuality

• Race and Ethnicity

• Urban and Spatial History

• Self-designed, in close consultation with major advisor
Students should select a concentration in consultation with their advisor. See the History Department website for suggested course coherence.

rules.name: Writing in the Major (WIM)
rules.notes:
This course may be taken in the junior or senior year, but not before completing the Sources and Methods seminar and Doing History colloquium. Students who wish to write an honors thesis are expected take course Research Seminar for Majors in their junior year.
course Research Seminar for Majors fulfills the WIM requirement only. It does not fulfill geographical requirements or small group course requirements.

rules.name: Capstone Experience
rules.desc: The History Department offers a range of options for students to complete the capstone requirement:

children.name: Honors Thesis
children.notes: Please note that the honors thesis does not contribute units toward the major, so students who choose to complete an honors thesis for the capstone requirement must take an additional course to reach the 13 course and 63 unit minimum.
children.desc: The Honors Thesis (See “Honors” below for more information.)

children.name: Capstone Course
children.desc: Students complete a capstone course in Autumn or Winter and then refine their projects in the 1-unit Creative Capstone Workshop in Spring Quarter.

children.name: Capstone Courses
children.desc: To be taken in Autumn or Winter Quarter.
children.notes: Other capstone course options will be added to this list as they become available.

children.name: Creative Capstone Workshop
children.desc: To be taken in Spring Quarter.
children.notes: Students must also present their project at the spring Creative Capstone Showcase.

children.name: Paper Revision or Expansion
children.notes:
A student who cannot take either course or course may petition to fulfill the capstone requirement by revising or expanding work previously done for a history course, either in consultation with the faculty member for whom the paper was originally written, or with a faculty advisor who will work as a team with the original faculty reader. Revision or expansion must constitute at least 20-25 pages of written work, or a re-conceptualized, non-paper equivalent as determined by the relevant faculty member(s).
Petitions to revise or expand work previously done for a history course must be submitted to the Director of Undergraduate Studies for review by the first day of the quarter in which the student intends to revise or expand previous work. Students whose petitions are approved must enroll in course to track completion as well as course. Students must also present their project at the spring Creative Capstone Showcase.
Please note that a paper revision or expansion does not contribute units toward the major, so students who choose to revise or expand a paper for the capstone requirement must take an additional course to reach the 13 course and 63 unit minimum.

rules.name: Honors (optional)
rules.desc:
To graduate with departmental honors in History, students must:

• Complete course Junior Honors Colloquium in the junior year. Students studying abroad during the winter quarter of their junior year are granted an automatic exemption from this requirement. Other exemptions are subject to the discretion of the Director of Honors.

• Complete HISTORY209S by the end of their junior year. Under rare circumstances, an exemption may be granted by the Director of Honors.

• Maintain a GPA of at least 3.3 in overall university work and a 3.5 in the History major during the final five quarters of enrollment/thesis preparation or obtain the consent of the director of the Honors Program.

• No later than autumn quarter of the senior year, select both an Advisor and a Second Reader who meet the eligibility criteria set forth in the department’s Honors Program Handbook

• Submit a completed honors thesis by the spring quarter deadline that meets submission requirements and receives a grade of B+ or above.

• Participate in mandatory Honors Program activities throughout the senior year (including, but not limited to, writing workshops and the annual honors thesis presentations) as specified in the Honors Program Handbook.
course Senior Research I, course Senior Research II, course Senior Research III do not fulfill any history major requirements other than honors, but the units count toward the 180 required for BA degree conferral.
